question.problem:
Which of the following vector spaces are finite-dimensional?

I. $C[0,1],$ the vector space of all continuous functions $f:[0,1]\to R$

II. ${\text{M}}_{200\times 300}(R),$ the vector space of all $200\times 300$ matrices over $R$

III. ${R}_{20}[t],$ the vector space of all polynomials in the variable $t$ of degree at most $20$
question.worked_solution:
Let's examine our vector spaces.

- $C[0,1]$ is *not* finite-dimensional. To understand why, we first note that the following set of (polynomial) functions is linearly independent:

$$
\{1,\,t,\,{t}^{2},\,…,{t}^{n}\},\,n\in N.
$$

Indeed, we have that 

$$
{\sum }_{i=0}^{n}{x}_{i}{t}^{i}=0
$$

for all $t\in [0,1]$ if and only if ${x}_{i}=0$ for all $i=0,1,2,…n.$ Therefore,  for any  $n\in N,$  there exists a linearly independent subset of $C[0,1]$ of size $n,$ which imples that $C[0,1]$ cannot have finite dimension.

- ${\text{M}}_{200\times 300}(R)$ and ${R}_{20}[t]$ are finite-dimensional. Indeed, 

$$
\text{dim}({\text{M}}_{200\times 300}(R))=200\cdot 300=60\,000,
$$

 
and

$$
\text{dim}({R}_{20}[t])=20+1=21
$$

are both finite numbers.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
